Theme

Church life · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

religious adjective

of a person: devout

also devout, pious, God-fearing

classical

Cic. Leg. 2.15: piōrum et impiōrum habēre ratiōnem (Lewis & Short)

pius, pia, pium

Declension on Wiktionary

devout, dutiful (towards God, parents, country)

Lewis & Short: “that performs what is due to the gods and religion in general, to parents, kindred … pious, devout, conscientious, affectionate”. Not only towards God: a dutiful son is pius too. The superlative piissimus is post-Augustan; Cicero called it no Latin at all (Phil. 13.43).

Other words

  • religiōsus, religiōsa, religiōsum — devout, God-fearing; scrupulous

    also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.72 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of persons, devout and careful in worship, and so scrupulous, conscientious; of places and things, sacred, or under a ban (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Religiōsior tū quidem es, quam prō aetāte. — Immō nūllam aetātem nōn decet religiō.

    “You are very devout for your age.” — “But there is no age that devotion does not suit.”Erasm. Coll., Pietās puerīlis (not classical)

  • piōrum et impiōrum habēre ratiōnem

    (that the gods) take account of the devout and the ungodlyCic. Leg. 2.15 (Lewis & Short)

See also religion, religious, pray, saint, Sunday school.
